questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That i was able to speak the local language (english) and that i wanted to explore the country and it's culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really receive any, other than an introduction to the Erasmus program and the university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay. I would recommend writing to one of the many student accommodations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try finding a spot close to campus or the city center, since public transportation is pretty bad in Cork.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just need to get a student card and register for classes, which is pretty straight forward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write and ask teachers or your contact persons for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful, but i was unable to have a lot of the classes that i wanted because they were held at the same time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You only get to know the schedule of the courses after you arrive, and then you get about a month to decide which courses you want and fit them together in a schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the teachers were very good, some very very bad.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was about the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was kind of the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Irish Literature
Sexuality and Society
Gender and Contemporary cinema
Irish Film History
Existentialism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Gender and Contemporary cinema was very interesting as well as Existentialism if you are into philosophy. Would NOT recommend Irish Film History, especially because the teaching was very bad.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When you move in you often have to buy a lot of stuff yourself (pots, pans, plates, cutlery, a cover for sleeping etc.)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries, bars and restaurants were as expensive as in Denmark which i did not contemplate.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sport clubs and societies. I think over a 100 in total, so lots of opportunities to meet new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played a lot af handball and went to matches with the team i Dublin which were very cool. I also joined Harry Potter society and Feminism society, but didn't have much time to engage with it as i had a lot of assignments.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take it easy and explore the city and surroundings on the weekends, and then go on a bigger trip once in a while. If you can, rent a car at least once as it is the best way to see Ireland, especially West Cork and Kerry which are incredible places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and ask what places they would recommend you to go to, and they might invite you along for a beer one day.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Its hard to say. Personally, I thought a lot of the Irish college students were a little superficial and immature, but maybe thats because of the age difference (they were mostly around 20 and I 24).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Irish are in general very sweet and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go alone, live in a student accommodation (even though it is expensive, it's worth it because it's easier being social) and join as much stuff as you can at the beginning. Since the stay is kind of short, you want to make friends early. Also, a lot of assignments will hit you after a couple of months, and you won't have as much time to make friends then.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to experience living in an other country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To complete all of the assignments and to be social at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
